v1_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-05), and this is not explained by slow response handling (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d, within 3.0d SLA; E-03) or a tariff change (0 logged changes; E-02, E-07). A measurable contributor is that manual meter-read route completion for ~9200 accounts fell to 88% vs a 95% target in Aug-Sep (E-04), which triggers estimate substitution that generates disputes: 1240 of 3025 disputed bills (41%) carry read_type ESTIMATED (E-01). The remaining 1785 disputed bills (59%, read_type ACTUAL) are not explained by estimate substitution, so the majority of the surge's cause is not yet established from committed evidence.
v2_problem: Billing dispute volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-05), unexplained by response-handling backlog (within SLA; E-03) or a tariff change (0 logged changes; E-02, E-07). The ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, 41%; E-01) is now fully traced to the billing-import pipeline: AMI firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) records registers in units of 0.1 m3 vs legacy m3 (E-13); rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 coincident with the surge onset, compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-14); this causes v4.2 AMI reads to be rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1184) or never received (56), summing exactly to the 1240 ESTIMATED bills (E-12) via estimate substitution. The remaining 1785 disputed bills (59%, ACTUAL read type; E-01) are not yet explained by this mechanism.
